parsed.why: Outed trans detainee faces birth-sex men's-system placement, prolonged isolation, forced strip searches, with no working remedy (tier 1). Society is strongly hostile (79% reject LGBT+ neighbours), hate-speech response weak, and legal gender change needs a psychiatric diagnosis. Some protections exist on paper and Pride is police-protected recently.

Same-sex conduct is criminalised and actively enforced (mass arrests, convictions). The president called for stoning, which reads as a licence to kill. No legal gender recognition, no anti-discrimination protection, and a broader crisis of extrajudicial killings and arbitrary detention.

No trans-specific criminal offence. Courts convicted assaults on trans tourists, police-violence conviction, and gender-change and asylum routes exist. Public-health coverage is documented. Downsides: hostile political rhetoric, dating-app entrapment of gay men, and a diffuse transphobia prevalence with no figure.

No criminalisation, but a 2026 police raid on an LGBTQ venue involved extortion and invented charges. Persecution reported after the 2024 election. No gender-recognition route and no hate-crime or anti-discrimination law. Thin record: the bulk of evidence is dated or national.

Tier-1 exposure: prisons place trans detainees by birth sex with isolation and strip-search exposure, which the custodial authority documented repeatedly with no marked improvement. Border ID friction documented. Strong offsets: aggravated-penalty and hate-speech laws, conversion-therapy ban, and funded care. Survey shows 64% discrimination.
